cards.definition:
An Account Admin operates at the Databricks account level, which sits above all workspaces. This role can:
1. Create and manage workspaces 2. Create and link Unity Catalog metastores 3. Assign workspace admin and account admin roles 4. Manage identity provisioning (SCIM, service principals, groups) 4. View and monitor account usage, audit logs, and system tables 5.Configure billing, subscription, serverless quotas, and previews

Metastores are the central governance backbone of Databricks Unity Catalog — the layer that controls how data is organized, secured, and accessed across all workspaces in your Databricks account. A metastore is a top‑level container in Unity Catalog that stores: 1. Catalogs 2. Schemas 3. Tables 4. Volumes 5. Permissions 6. External locations 7. Data lineage metadata

The Metastore Administrator (often called Metastore Admin) is a high‑privilege Unity Catalog role that governs all data objects inside a single Databricks metastore. It sits below the Account Admin but above Workspace Admins in terms of data-governance authority.

The Workspace Administrator (Workspace Admin) is the primary operational admin role inside a single Databricks workspace. If the Account Admin governs the whole account and the Metastore Admin governs data, the Workspace Admin governs the environment where people actually work—clusters, jobs, notebooks, repos, permissions, and workspace-level identities.

The Owner role in Databricks is one of the most powerful object‑level permissions in Unity Catalog. Unlike Account Admin or Workspace Admin—which govern environments—the Owner role governs a specific object (catalog, schema, table, volume, view, function, etc.) and gives full control over that object.
it’s a standard way to automatically create, update, and remove user accounts across different systems.
A Resource Group (RG) is a logical container that holds Azure resources—VMs, storage accounts, VNets, databases, anything.
An Azure private subnet keeps your data systems off the public internet. You need Databricks when you want to process, transform, analyze, or govern the data inside those private subnets at scale.
An Azure public subnet exposes resources to the internet (with public IPs).

A Databricks workspace is the core environment where all your data engineering, analytics, and machine‑learning work actually happens. A workspace is a fully managed development environment that contains: 1. Notebooks (Python, SQL, Scala, R) 2. Clusters (compute) 3. Jobs (scheduled pipelines) 4. Repos (Git integration) 5. Dashboards 6. Data access (Unity Catalog) 7. MLflow experiments & models

Databricks Account Console Workspaces are the cloud environments you create from the Databricks Account Console to run notebooks, jobs, SQL warehouses, pipelines, dashboards, and ML workloads. They are the “rooms” where people actually work, while the Account Console is the control plane that manages all of them.

A Databricks Account Console Catalog is not a separate object type inside the Account Console. Instead, the Account Console manages Unity Catalog metastores, and catalogs are objects inside those metastores. So when someone says “Account Console Catalog,” they are referring to catalogs as they appear in the Account Console’s governance layer (Unity Catalog).

Databricks Account Console User Management is the centralized identity and access control layer for your entire Databricks account. It’s where Account Admins manage who can access Databricks, what roles they have, and which workspaces they belong to — all from one unified control plane.

This is one of the most important parts of Databricks governance because it ensures consistent identity, security, and compliance across every workspace.

Databricks Account Console Cloud Resources refers to the cloud infrastructure configurations that Account Admins manage at the account level to support workspace deployment, networking, storage, compute credentials, and secure connectivity. These resources define how Databricks integrates with your cloud provider (AWS, Azure, GCP) and are required for classic workspaces, private networking, and secure data access.

Databricks Account Console Previews are the early‑access, account‑level feature toggles that let Account Admins enable new Databricks capabilities before they become generally available (GA). They act as a controlled way to test upcoming platform features across workspaces, governance layers, and cloud integrations.

They’re essentially the feature flags for the Databricks platform — but only at the account layer, not workspace settings.

Databricks Account Console Settings is the central configuration hub for your entire Databricks account. It’s where Account Admins control global behaviors, security posture, feature availability, and platform-wide defaults that apply across all workspaces and metastores.

If the Account Console is the “control plane,” then Settings is the “master switchboard.”
